claims.text: AlxCoCrFeNi alloys with 1.0 ≤ x ≤ 2.0 are multiphase high-entropy alloys containing FCC, BCC, and ordered derivative phases.
These alloys will exhibit a ductile-brittle-ductile transition during aging at 400–600 °C.
The non-monotonic ductility transition is caused by competing evolution of short-range order and long-range order within the B2 phase.
The initial alloys possess short-range order around Al atoms.
The initial B2 phase has negligible long-range order.
Aging for 100–10,000 hours at 400–600 °C induces chemical ordering and phase separation.
Ordering evolves sequentially from a disordered state to SRO and then to nucleation and growth of B2 LRO.
Prolonged aging produces Ni/Co/Al-rich B2 regions and Fe/Cr-rich disordered regions.
Increasing SRO facilitates cross-slip and dislocation accumulation.
SRO-mediated cross-slip and dislocation accumulation increase ductility.
Strong B2 LRO restricts dislocation motion and promotes brittle cleavage.
Phase separation or saturation of LRO restores ductility by creating disordered Fe/Cr-rich deformation paths.
Elongation to failure initially increases, reaches a sharp minimum at peak LRO, and then increases at longer aging times.
Higher Al contents favor a late-stage ductility recovery associated with phase separation.
As-cast AlxCoCrFeNi alloys typically exhibit 10–20% elongation, depending on Al content.
FCC AlxCoCrFeNi alloys are more ductile than BCC AlxCoCrFeNi alloys.
The ordering onset temperature rises from approximately 1220 °C at x = 1 to approximately 1850 °C at x = 2.
B2 ordering is thermodynamically favorable primarily when x ≥ 1.0.
The transition is unlikely in alloys with x < 1 or in BCC alloys lacking Al enrichment.

contradictions.description: The initial state is said to contain an ordered B2 phase while also having negligible LRO in that phase, and the mediator is described as evolving from a disordered state into B2 LRO. Calling a phase B2 ordinarily implies long-range chemical order, so these descriptions are internally inconsistent without a distinction between B2-like composition and genuinely ordered B2.

The core hypothesis defines a transition with aging time, but the predicted recovery is alternatively assigned to higher Al content. A composition-dependent comparison does not by itself establish the third stage of a time-dependent ductile-brittle-ductile transition.
